pt.title: [Logística 101 #8] O caminhão mais barato é o que não volta vazio

segments.src: > Transportation management is three decisions stacked on top of each other: how you move it (mode), what you pay for it (rate structure), and the order you touch the stops (routing) — and the third one is usually where the money hides.
segments.tr: > A gestão de transporte são três decisões empilhadas: como movimentar (modal), quanto pagar (estrutura de tarifas) e a ordem em que você visita as paradas (roteirização). E a terceira costuma ser onde o dinheiro se esconde.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: Transportation is the single biggest line item in most supply chains.
segments.tr: O transporte é o maior item de custo na maioria das cadeias de suprimentos.

segments.src: In the U.S., freight transportation runs well over a trillion dollars a year, and for a typical consumer-goods company, moving product costs more than warehousing it.
segments.tr: Nos EUA, o transporte de cargas movimenta bem mais de um trilhão de dólares por ano, e, para uma empresa típica de bens de consumo, movimentar produtos custa mais do que armazená-los.

segments.src: So "transportation management" isn't a back-office chore.
segments.tr: Por isso, "gestão de transporte" não é uma tarefa de retaguarda.

segments.src: It's a series of trade-offs a manager makes on purpose.
segments.tr: É uma série de trade-offs que o gestor faz de propósito.

segments.src: **Decision 1: The mode.** Modes line up in a predictable order on cost per ton-mile — pipeline and barge cheapest, then rail, then truck, then air.
segments.tr: **Decisão 1: O modal.** Os modais se alinham em uma ordem previsível pelo custo por tonelada-milha: dutovia e barcaça são os mais baratos, depois ferrovia, depois caminhão, depois avião.

segments.src: Speed lines up in exactly the reverse order.
segments.tr: A velocidade segue exatamente a ordem inversa.

segments.src: That inversion is the whole game.
segments.tr: Essa inversão é o cerne do jogo.

segments.src: Air freight can cost 5–10x truck per pound but delivers in a day; ocean can cost a fraction of air but takes weeks.
segments.tr: O frete aéreo pode custar de 5 a 10 vezes o do caminhão por quilo, mas entrega em um dia; o marítimo custa uma fração do aéreo, mas leva semanas.

segments.src: You aren't picking the "best" mode, you're picking where on that curve your product belongs.
segments.tr: Você não escolhe o modal "melhor", e sim o ponto dessa curva onde o seu produto se encaixa.

segments.src: Fresh strawberries and replacement heart valves ride at the fast end.
segments.tr: Morangos frescos e válvulas cardíacas de reposição ficam na ponta rápida.

segments.src: Gravel and canned beans ride at the cheap end.
segments.tr: Cascalho e feijão enlatado ficam na ponta barata.

segments.src: Within trucking there's a second fork most people never see:
segments.tr: Dentro do rodoviário há uma segunda bifurcação que a maioria nunca percebe:

segments.src: - **Parcel** — anything roughly under 150 lbs, one box at a time (UPS, FedEx, USPS).
segments.tr: - **Encomenda (parcel)**: qualquer coisa de até cerca de 150 libras, uma caixa de cada vez (UPS, FedEx, USPS).

segments.src: - **LTL (less-than-truckload)** — a few pallets sharing a trailer with other shippers' freight, moving through terminal hubs.
segments.tr: - **LTL (less-than-truckload)**: alguns paletes dividindo o baú com cargas de outros embarcadores, passando por hubs de terminais.

segments.src: - **TL / FTL (truckload)** — you buy the whole trailer, and it drives point to point.
segments.tr: - **TL / FTL (truckload)**: você compra o baú inteiro, e ele roda de ponto a ponto.

segments.src: - **Intermodal** — the container rides a train for the long middle, and a truck for the first and last 100 miles.
segments.tr: - **Intermodal**: o contêiner vai de trem no trecho longo do meio e de caminhão nos primeiros e últimos 100 milhas.

segments.src: **Decision 2: The rate structure.** A freight invoice is almost never one number.
segments.tr: **Decisão 2: A estrutura de tarifas.** Uma fatura de frete quase nunca é um número só.

segments.src: It's a stack:
segments.tr: Ela é uma pilha:

segments.src: total = linehaul + fuel surcharge + accessorials + minimum charge floor
segments.tr: total = linehaul + fuel surcharge + accessorials + minimum charge floor

segments.src: *Linehaul* is the base move (distance × weight × lane).
segments.tr: *Linehaul* é o deslocamento base (distância × peso × rota).

segments.src: *Fuel surcharge* floats with a published diesel index — the DOE/EIA weekly average — so carriers don't have to re-quote every time fuel moves.
segments.tr: *Sobretaxa de combustível* acompanha um índice publicado de diesel, a média semanal do DOE/EIA, para que as transportadoras não precisem recotar toda vez que o combustível muda.

segments.src: *Accessorials* are the add-ons: liftgate, residential delivery, inside delivery, detention when your dock makes the driver wait, redelivery when nobody's there.
segments.tr: *Taxas acessórias* são os adicionais: plataforma elevatória (liftgate), entrega residencial, entrega interna, estadia (detention) quando sua doca faz o motorista esperar, reentrega quando não há ninguém no local.

segments.src: Accessorials are where budgets quietly bleed, because nobody quotes them and everybody pays them.
segments.tr: As taxas acessórias são onde os orçamentos sangram sem que ninguém perceba, porque ninguém as cota e todos as pagam.

segments.src: Two pricing quirks worth knowing.
segments.tr: Duas peculiaridades de preço valem ser conhecidas.

segments.src: First, **dimensional weight**: carriers bill on whichever is greater, actual weight or volume converted to weight.
segments.tr: Primeiro, o **peso dimensional**: as transportadoras cobram pelo que for maior, o peso real ou o volume convertido em peso.

segments.src: A big box of pillows takes up trailer space the carrier can't resell, so they charge for the space.
segments.tr: Uma caixa grande de travesseiros ocupa espaço no baú que a transportadora não consegue revender, então ela cobra pelo espaço.

segments.src: dim weight (lbs) = (L x W x H in inches) / divisor     # 139 is common for U.S. parcel
segments.tr: dim weight (lbs) = (L x W x H in inches) / divisor     # 139 is common for U.S. parcel

segments.src: Second, **freight class**: LTL freight is classified 50 through 500 based on density, stowability, handling, and liability.
segments.tr: Segundo, a **classe de frete**: a carga LTL é classificada de 50 a 500 com base em densidade, facilidade de acomodação, manuseio e responsabilidade.

segments.src: Class 50 (dense, sturdy, boring — think bricks) is cheap.
segments.tr: A classe 50 (densa, resistente, sem graça, pense em tijolos) é barata.

segments.src: Class 500 (light, bulky, fragile — think ping-pong balls) is expensive.
segments.tr: A classe 500 (leve, volumosa, frágil, pense em bolinhas de pingue-pongue) é cara.

segments.src: Same trailer, same 500 miles, wildly different bill.
segments.tr: Mesmo baú, mesmas 500 milhas, contas radicalmente diferentes.

segments.src: **Decision 3: The route.** This is the hardest one and the most under-managed.
segments.tr: **Decisão 3: A rota.** Esta é a mais difícil e a menos gerenciada.

segments.src: Deciding what order to hit 10 stops in isn't a small problem — with a fixed starting depot, there are 10!
segments.tr: Decidir em que ordem visitar 10 paradas não é um problema pequeno: com um depósito inicial fixo, há 10!

segments.src: ÷ 2 ≈ **1.8 million** possible route orders.
segments.tr: ÷ 2 ≈ **1,8 milhão** de ordens de rota possíveis.

segments.src: Add 20 stops and the count exceeds the number of atoms you'd care to count.
segments.tr: Com 20 paradas, a contagem supera o número de átomos que você se daria ao trabalho de contar.

segments.src: Computer scientists call this family of problems the Traveling Salesman Problem and its bigger sibling the Vehicle Routing Problem, and both are NP-hard: nobody checks every option, so real software uses heuristics that find a very good route fast rather than the perfect one slowly.
segments.tr: Cientistas da computação chamam essa família de problemas de Problema do Caixeiro Viajante, e seu irmão maior, o Problema de Roteirização de Veículos; ambos são NP-difíceis: ninguém testa todas as opções, então softwares reais usam heurísticas que encontram uma rota muito boa rapidamente, em vez da rota perfeita lentamente.

segments.src: Routing also means killing empty miles.
segments.tr: Roteirizar também significa eliminar milhas vazias.

segments.src: A truck driving back to base with nothing in it is **deadhead** — full cost, zero revenue.
segments.tr: Um caminhão voltando à base sem carga está em **deadhead**: custo total, receita zero.

segments.src: Roughly a sixth of U.S.
segments.tr: Cerca de um sexto das

segments.src: truck miles run empty.
segments.tr: milhas de caminhão nos EUA rodam vazias.

segments.src: Finding a **backhaul** (paying freight for the return leg) is often a bigger win than shaving a nickel off the outbound rate.
segments.tr: Encontrar um **backhaul** (pagar frete pelo trecho de volta) costuma render mais do que reduzir alguns centavos na tarifa de ida.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## No Dia a Dia

segments.src: Say you run a small cold-brew coffee company in Portland, Oregon, and you just landed a Chicago account.
segments.tr: Suponha que você administre uma pequena empresa de café cold brew em Portland, Oregon, e tenha acabado de fechar uma conta em Chicago.

segments.src: Six pallets, 3,600 lbs total, and it needs to be there in a week.
segments.tr: Seis paletes, 3.600 libras no total, e precisam chegar em uma semana.

segments.src: Your options, roughly (illustrative numbers, not quotes):
segments.tr: Suas opções, em linhas gerais (números ilustrativos, não cotações):

segments.src: - **Parcel**: ship it as ~300 individual cases. Fast, trackable, and you'd pay something like $3,000+ once dim weight kicks in. Parcel punishes you for volume.
segments.tr: - **Encomenda**: enviar cerca de 300 caixas individuais. Rápido, rastreável, e você pagaria algo como US$ 3.000+ assim que o peso dimensional entrar em cena. A encomenda penaliza o volume.

segments.src: - **LTL**: six pallets on a shared trailer, ~5–7 days through terminal hubs. Maybe $1,400. But your customer's Lincoln Park storefront has no dock, so add a liftgate fee (~$100) and a limited-access delivery fee (~$90). Your $1,400 quote is a $1,600 invoice.
segments.tr: - **LTL**: seis paletes em um baú compartilhado, cerca de 5 a 7 dias passando por hubs de terminais. Talvez US$ 1.400. Mas a loja do seu cliente em Lincoln Park não tem doca, então some uma taxa de plataforma elevatória (~US$ 100) e uma taxa de entrega em área de acesso restrito (~US$ 90). Seu orçamento de US$ 1.400 vira uma fatura de US$ 1.600.

segments.src: - **Truckload**: you'd buy 2,100 miles of trailer for maybe $4,000. Insane for six pallets — you'd be paying for 20 pallets of empty air.
segments.tr: - **Carga fechada (TL)**: você compraria 2.100 milhas de baú por talvez US$ 4.000. Absurdo para seis paletes: você estaria pagando por 20 paletes de ar vazio.

segments.src: - **Intermodal**: cheapest per mile, but the container-load economics don't work at six pallets, and the extra transit days eat your buffer.
segments.tr: - **Intermodal**: o mais barato por milha, mas a economia de contêiner completo não funciona com seis paletes, e os dias extras de trânsito consomem sua margem de segurança.

segments.src: LTL wins.
segments.tr: O LTL vence.

segments.src: But notice *why* it wins: not because it's fast or cheap in the abstract, but because your shipment size fell in its sweet spot.
segments.tr: Mas repare em *por que* ele vence: não porque é rápido ou barato em abstrato, e sim porque o tamanho do seu embarque caiu na faixa ideal dele.

segments.src: Double the order to 14 pallets and truckload suddenly beats it on cost per pallet — that's the classic **LTL/TL breakeven**, usually somewhere around 8–14 pallets depending on the lane.
segments.tr: Dobre o pedido para 14 paletes e a carga fechada passa a ganhar em custo por palete. Esse é o clássico **ponto de equilíbrio LTL/TL**, geralmente entre 8 e 14 paletes, dependendo da rota.

segments.src: Now the routing half.
segments.tr: Agora, a parte da roteirização.

segments.src: Once you're delivering to 40 Chicago-area accounts yourself, the question stops being "what's my rate?"
segments.tr: Quando você mesmo estiver entregando para 40 clientes na região de Chicago, a pergunta deixa de ser "qual é a minha tarifa?"

segments.src: and becomes "what order do I drive?"
segments.tr: e passa a ser "em que ordem eu dirijo?"

segments.src: UPS's ORION routing system is the famous version of this: by optimizing driver routes — including the well-known habit of minimizing left turns, which waste time idling in traffic and raise collision risk — UPS has said it saves on the order of 100 million miles a year.
segments.tr: O sistema de roteirização ORION da UPS é a versão famosa disso: otimizando as rotas dos motoristas, incluindo o hábito bem conhecido de minimizar as curvas à esquerda, que desperdiçam tempo parados no trânsito e aumentam o risco de colisão, a UPS afirma que economiza algo na ordem de 100 milhões de milhas por ano.

segments.src: Nobody negotiated a better fuel price.
segments.tr: Ninguém negociou um preço de combustível melhor.

segments.src: They just drove better sequences.
segments.tr: Eles apenas dirigiram sequências melhores.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumo em Três Linhas

segments.src: 1. Mode choice is a speed-versus-cost trade: pipeline → rail → truck → air gets faster and more expensive at every step, so match the mode to what the product's time is actually worth.
segments.tr: 1. A escolha do modal é um trade-off entre velocidade e custo: dutovia → ferrovia → caminhão → avião fica mais rápido e mais caro a cada passo, então combine o modal com o valor real que o tempo do produto tem.

segments.src: 2. Freight rates are a stack — linehaul, fuel surcharge, accessorials, minimums — and volume-based pricing (dim weight, freight class) means bulky-but-light freight pays like heavy freight.
segments.tr: 2. As tarifas de frete são uma pilha (linehaul, sobretaxa de combustível, taxas acessórias, mínimos), e a precificação por volume (peso dimensional, classe de frete) faz com que carga volumosa porém leve pague como carga pesada.

segments.src: 3. Routing is a combinatorial problem solved by heuristics, and the biggest lever is usually eliminating empty miles, not shaving the base rate.
segments.tr: 3. A roteirização é um problema combinatório resolvido por heurísticas, e a maior alavanca costuma ser eliminar milhas vazias, e não reduzir a tarifa base.

segments.tr: - **Intermodal**: movimentar um contêiner por dois ou mais modais (normalmente ferrovia no trecho longo e caminhão nas pontas) sem desembalá-lo.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** Packing peanuts are extremely low-density, so carriers bill on the space consumed rather than the scale weight (dim weight in parcel, high freight class in LTL).

segments.src: **2 — False.** TL only wins once your shipment is large enough to justify buying the whole trailer; below the breakeven (commonly ~8–14 pallets), you'd be paying to haul empty space, and LTL's shared-trailer model is cheaper.
segments.tr: **2 — Falso.** A carga fechada só compensa quando o embarque é grande o suficiente para justificar a compra do baú inteiro; abaixo do ponto de equilíbrio (comumente ~8 a 14 paletes), você pagaria para transportar espaço vazio, e o modelo de baú compartilhado do LTL é mais barato.

segments.src: **3 — C.** Empty return miles are deadhead, and the standard remedy is securing a backhaul — paying freight for the return leg — which is often a larger saving than negotiating the outbound rate down.*
segments.tr: **3 — C.** As milhas de retorno vazias são deadhead, e o remédio padrão é garantir um backhaul (pagar frete pelo trecho de volta), que costuma gerar economia maior do que negociar a tarifa de ida para baixo.*

in.title: [Logistik 101 #8] Truk Termurah Adalah Truk yang Tidak Kembali dalam Keadaan Kosong

segments.src: > Transportation management is three decisions stacked on top of each other: how you move it (mode), what you pay for it (rate structure), and the order you touch the stops (routing) — and the third one is usually where the money hides.
segments.tr: > Manajemen transportasi terdiri dari tiga keputusan yang saling bertumpuk: bagaimana memindahkannya (moda), berapa biayanya (struktur tarif), dan urutan singgah di setiap titik (rute). Keputusan ketiga biasanya tempat uang tersembunyi.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Transportation is the single biggest line item in most supply chains.
segments.tr: Transportasi adalah pos biaya terbesar dalam sebagian besar rantai pasok.

segments.src: In the U.S., freight transportation runs well over a trillion dollars a year, and for a typical consumer-goods company, moving product costs more than warehousing it.
segments.tr: Di AS, angkutan barang mencapai lebih dari satu triliun dolar per tahun, dan bagi perusahaan barang konsumen pada umumnya, memindahkan produk lebih mahal daripada menyimpannya di gudang.

segments.src: So "transportation management" isn't a back-office chore.
segments.tr: Jadi "manajemen transportasi" bukan pekerjaan administratif biasa.

segments.src: It's a series of trade-offs a manager makes on purpose.
segments.tr: Ini adalah serangkaian pertimbangan yang sengaja diambil oleh seorang manajer.

segments.src: **Decision 1: The mode.** Modes line up in a predictable order on cost per ton-mile — pipeline and barge cheapest, then rail, then truck, then air.
segments.tr: **Keputusan 1: Moda.** Moda tersusun dalam urutan yang dapat diprediksi berdasarkan biaya per ton-mil: pipa dan tongkang paling murah, lalu kereta api, truk, dan udara.

segments.src: Speed lines up in exactly the reverse order.
segments.tr: Kecepatannya tersusun dalam urutan yang persis terbalik.

segments.src: That inversion is the whole game.
segments.tr: Pembalikan inilah inti permainannya.

segments.src: Air freight can cost 5–10x truck per pound but delivers in a day; ocean can cost a fraction of air but takes weeks.
segments.tr: Angkutan udara bisa berbiaya 5–10 kali lipat truk per pon, tetapi tiba dalam sehari. Angkutan laut bisa berbiaya sebagian kecil dari udara, tetapi memakan waktu berminggu-minggu.

segments.src: You aren't picking the "best" mode, you're picking where on that curve your product belongs.
segments.tr: Anda tidak memilih moda yang "terbaik", melainkan menentukan di titik mana pada kurva itu produk Anda seharusnya berada.

segments.src: Fresh strawberries and replacement heart valves ride at the fast end.
segments.tr: Stroberi segar dan katup jantung pengganti menggunakan ujung yang cepat.

segments.src: Gravel and canned beans ride at the cheap end.
segments.tr: Kerikil dan kacang kalengan menggunakan ujung yang murah.

segments.src: Within trucking there's a second fork most people never see:
segments.tr: Dalam angkutan truk ada cabang kedua yang jarang disadari kebanyakan orang:

segments.src: - **Parcel** — anything roughly under 150 lbs, one box at a time (UPS, FedEx, USPS).
segments.tr: - **Parsel**: apa pun yang kurang lebih di bawah 150 pon, satu kotak per satu kali (UPS, FedEx, USPS).

segments.src: - **LTL (less-than-truckload)** — a few pallets sharing a trailer with other shippers' freight, moving through terminal hubs.
segments.tr: - **LTL (less-than-truckload)**: beberapa palet yang berbagi trailer dengan kiriman pengirim lain, bergerak melalui hub terminal.

segments.src: - **TL / FTL (truckload)** — you buy the whole trailer, and it drives point to point.
segments.tr: - **TL / FTL (truckload)**: Anda membeli seluruh trailer, dan trailer itu berjalan langsung dari titik asal ke tujuan.

segments.src: - **Intermodal** — the container rides a train for the long middle, and a truck for the first and last 100 miles.
segments.tr: - **Intermodal**: kontainer naik kereta untuk bagian jarak jauh, dan truk untuk 100 mil pertama dan terakhir.

segments.src: **Decision 2: The rate structure.** A freight invoice is almost never one number.
segments.tr: **Keputusan 2: Struktur tarif.** Faktur angkutan hampir tidak pernah berupa satu angka.

segments.src: It's a stack:
segments.tr: Melainkan tumpukan:

segments.src: total = linehaul + fuel surcharge + accessorials + minimum charge floor
segments.tr: total = linehaul + fuel surcharge + accessorials + minimum charge floor

segments.src: *Linehaul* is the base move (distance × weight × lane).
segments.tr: *Linehaul* adalah perjalanan dasar (jarak × berat × lajur).

segments.src: *Fuel surcharge* floats with a published diesel index — the DOE/EIA weekly average — so carriers don't have to re-quote every time fuel moves.
segments.tr: *Surcharge bahan bakar* mengikuti indeks solar yang dipublikasikan, yaitu rata-rata mingguan DOE/EIA, sehingga perusahaan angkutan tidak perlu menghitung ulang penawaran setiap kali harga BBM berubah.

segments.src: *Accessorials* are the add-ons: liftgate, residential delivery, inside delivery, detention when your dock makes the driver wait, redelivery when nobody's there.
segments.tr: *Aksesori* adalah biaya tambahan: liftgate, pengiriman ke rumah tinggal, pengiriman sampai ke dalam, detensi ketika dermaga Anda membuat sopir menunggu, dan pengiriman ulang ketika tidak ada yang di tempat.

segments.src: Accessorials are where budgets quietly bleed, because nobody quotes them and everybody pays them.
segments.tr: Aksesori adalah tempat anggaran diam-diam bocor, karena tidak ada yang menawarkannya tetapi semua orang membayarnya.

segments.src: Two pricing quirks worth knowing.
segments.tr: Ada dua keunikan harga yang layak diketahui.

segments.src: First, **dimensional weight**: carriers bill on whichever is greater, actual weight or volume converted to weight.
segments.tr: Pertama, **berat dimensi**: perusahaan angkutan menagih berdasarkan mana yang lebih besar, berat aktual atau volume yang dikonversi menjadi berat.

segments.src: A big box of pillows takes up trailer space the carrier can't resell, so they charge for the space.
segments.tr: Kotak besar berisi bantal memakan ruang trailer yang tidak bisa dijual kembali oleh perusahaan angkutan, jadi mereka menagih ruang itu.

segments.src: dim weight (lbs) = (L x W x H in inches) / divisor     # 139 is common for U.S. parcel
segments.tr: dim weight (lbs) = (L x W x H in inches) / divisor     # 139 is common for U.S. parcel

segments.src: Second, **freight class**: LTL freight is classified 50 through 500 based on density, stowability, handling, and liability.
segments.tr: Kedua, **kelas angkutan**: barang LTL digolongkan dalam kelas 50 hingga 500 berdasarkan kepadatan, kemudahan penyusunan, penanganan, dan tanggung jawab.

segments.src: Class 50 (dense, sturdy, boring — think bricks) is cheap.
segments.tr: Kelas 50 (padat, kokoh, membosankan, bayangkan batu bata) itu murah.

segments.src: Class 500 (light, bulky, fragile — think ping-pong balls) is expensive.
segments.tr: Kelas 500 (ringan, besar, rapuh, bayangkan bola pingpong) itu mahal.

segments.src: Same trailer, same 500 miles, wildly different bill.
segments.tr: Trailer yang sama, jarak 500 mil yang sama, tetapi tagihannya sangat berbeda.

segments.src: **Decision 3: The route.** This is the hardest one and the most under-managed.
segments.tr: **Keputusan 3: Rute.** Ini yang paling sulit dan paling sedikit dikelola.

segments.src: Deciding what order to hit 10 stops in isn't a small problem — with a fixed starting depot, there are 10!
segments.tr: Menentukan urutan untuk mendatangi 10 titik bukanlah masalah kecil. Dengan depot awal yang tetap, ada 10!

segments.src: ÷ 2 ≈ **1.8 million** possible route orders.
segments.tr: ÷ 2 ≈ **1,8 juta** kemungkinan urutan rute.

segments.src: Add 20 stops and the count exceeds the number of atoms you'd care to count.
segments.tr: Tambahkan 20 titik dan jumlahnya melampaui jumlah atom yang mungkin ingin Anda hitung.

segments.src: Computer scientists call this family of problems the Traveling Salesman Problem and its bigger sibling the Vehicle Routing Problem, and both are NP-hard: nobody checks every option, so real software uses heuristics that find a very good route fast rather than the perfect one slowly.
segments.tr: Ilmuwan komputer menyebut keluarga masalah ini Traveling Salesman Problem, dan saudaranya yang lebih besar Vehicle Routing Problem. Keduanya NP-hard: tidak ada yang memeriksa setiap opsi, jadi perangkat lunak sungguhan menggunakan heuristik yang menemukan rute yang sangat baik dengan cepat, bukan rute yang sempurna dengan lambat.

segments.src: Routing also means killing empty miles.
segments.tr: Perutean juga berarti memangkas perjalanan kosong.

segments.src: A truck driving back to base with nothing in it is **deadhead** — full cost, zero revenue.
segments.tr: Truk yang kembali ke basis tanpa muatan adalah **deadhead**: biaya penuh, tanpa pendapatan.

segments.src: Roughly a sixth of U.S.
segments.tr: Sekitar seperenam mil truk di AS

segments.src: truck miles run empty.
segments.tr: berjalan dalam keadaan kosong.

segments.src: Finding a **backhaul** (paying freight for the return leg) is often a bigger win than shaving a nickel off the outbound rate.
segments.tr: Menemukan **backhaul** (membayar angkutan untuk perjalanan pulang) sering kali lebih menguntungkan daripada memangkas tarif perjalanan berangkat beberapa sen.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: Say you run a small cold-brew coffee company in Portland, Oregon, and you just landed a Chicago account.
segments.tr: Misalkan Anda menjalankan perusahaan kopi cold brew kecil di Portland, Oregon, dan baru saja mendapatkan klien di Chicago.

segments.src: Six pallets, 3,600 lbs total, and it needs to be there in a week.
segments.tr: Enam palet, total 3.600 pon, dan harus sampai dalam seminggu.

segments.src: Your options, roughly (illustrative numbers, not quotes):
segments.tr: Pilihan Anda, kira-kira (angka ilustratif, bukan penawaran):

segments.src: - **Parcel**: ship it as ~300 individual cases. Fast, trackable, and you'd pay something like $3,000+ once dim weight kicks in. Parcel punishes you for volume.
segments.tr: - **Parsel**: kirim sekitar 300 kotak terpisah. Cepat, dapat dilacak, dan Anda akan membayar sekitar $3.000+ setelah berat dimensi berlaku. Parsel menghukum Anda karena volume.

segments.src: - **LTL**: six pallets on a shared trailer, ~5–7 days through terminal hubs. Maybe $1,400. But your customer's Lincoln Park storefront has no dock, so add a liftgate fee (~$100) and a limited-access delivery fee (~$90). Your $1,400 quote is a $1,600 invoice.
segments.tr: - **LTL**: enam palet di trailer bersama, sekitar 5–7 hari melalui hub terminal. Mungkin $1.400. Namun toko klien Anda di Lincoln Park tidak punya dok, jadi tambahkan biaya liftgate (~$100) dan biaya pengiriman akses terbatas (~$90). Penawaran $1.400 Anda menjadi faktur $1.600.

segments.src: - **Truckload**: you'd buy 2,100 miles of trailer for maybe $4,000. Insane for six pallets — you'd be paying for 20 pallets of empty air.
segments.tr: - **Truckload**: Anda akan membeli 2.100 mil trailer seharga sekitar $4.000. Tidak masuk akal untuk enam palet, karena Anda membayar 20 palet udara kosong.

segments.src: - **Intermodal**: cheapest per mile, but the container-load economics don't work at six pallets, and the extra transit days eat your buffer.
segments.tr: - **Intermodal**: paling murah per mil, tetapi ekonomi muatan kontainer tidak berjalan dengan enam palet, dan tambahan hari transit menghabiskan penyangga Anda.

segments.src: LTL wins.
segments.tr: LTL menang.

segments.src: But notice *why* it wins: not because it's fast or cheap in the abstract, but because your shipment size fell in its sweet spot.
segments.tr: Namun perhatikan *mengapa* ia menang: bukan karena cepat atau murah secara umum, melainkan karena ukuran pengiriman Anda berada di titik manisnya.

segments.src: Double the order to 14 pallets and truckload suddenly beats it on cost per pallet — that's the classic **LTL/TL breakeven**, usually somewhere around 8–14 pallets depending on the lane.
segments.tr: Gandakan pesanan menjadi 14 palet dan truckload tiba-tiba mengalahkannya dalam biaya per palet. Itulah **titik impas LTL/TL** klasik, biasanya sekitar 8–14 palet tergantung lajurnya.

segments.src: Now the routing half.
segments.tr: Sekarang bagian rutenya.

segments.src: Once you're delivering to 40 Chicago-area accounts yourself, the question stops being "what's my rate?"
segments.tr: Begitu Anda mengirim ke 40 klien di area Chicago sendiri, pertanyaannya tidak lagi "berapa tarif saya?"

segments.src: and becomes "what order do I drive?"
segments.tr: melainkan "urutan mana yang harus saya tempuh?"

segments.src: UPS's ORION routing system is the famous version of this: by optimizing driver routes — including the well-known habit of minimizing left turns, which waste time idling in traffic and raise collision risk — UPS has said it saves on the order of 100 million miles a year.
segments.tr: Sistem perutean ORION milik UPS adalah versi terkenal dari ini. Dengan mengoptimalkan rute pengemudi, termasuk kebiasaan terkenal untuk meminimalkan belokan kiri (yang membuang waktu saat mesin menyala di kemacetan dan meningkatkan risiko tabrakan), UPS menyatakan menghemat sekitar 100 juta mil per tahun.

segments.src: Nobody negotiated a better fuel price.
segments.tr: Tidak ada yang menegosiasikan harga bahan bakar yang lebih baik.

segments.src: They just drove better sequences.
segments.tr: Mereka hanya mengemudi dengan urutan yang lebih baik.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Rekap Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. Mode choice is a speed-versus-cost trade: pipeline → rail → truck → air gets faster and more expensive at every step, so match the mode to what the product's time is actually worth.
segments.tr: 1. Pemilihan moda adalah pertukaran antara kecepatan dan biaya: pipa → kereta api → truk → udara semakin cepat dan semakin mahal di setiap langkah, jadi sesuaikan moda dengan nilai waktu produk Anda yang sebenarnya.

segments.src: 2. Freight rates are a stack — linehaul, fuel surcharge, accessorials, minimums — and volume-based pricing (dim weight, freight class) means bulky-but-light freight pays like heavy freight.
segments.tr: 2. Tarif angkutan adalah tumpukan (linehaul, surcharge bahan bakar, aksesori, minimum). Harga berbasis volume (berat dimensi, kelas angkutan) berarti barang besar tapi ringan dibayar seperti barang berat.

segments.src: 3. Routing is a combinatorial problem solved by heuristics, and the biggest lever is usually eliminating empty miles, not shaving the base rate.
segments.tr: 3. Perutean adalah masalah kombinatorial yang diselesaikan dengan heuristik, dan tuas terbesarnya biasanya adalah menghilangkan perjalanan kosong, bukan memangkas tarif dasar.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.src: **1.** You're shipping 800 lbs of foam packing peanuts across the country.
segments.tr: **1.** Anda mengirim 800 pon isian busa kemasan lintas negara.

segments.src: Which pricing mechanism will most likely drive your cost above what the scale weight suggests?
segments.tr: Mekanisme harga mana yang paling mungkin membuat biaya Anda melampaui berat timbangan?

segments.src: - A) Fuel surcharge
segments.tr: - A) Surcharge bahan bakar

segments.src: - B) Dimensional weight / high freight class
segments.tr: - B) Berat dimensi / kelas angkutan tinggi

segments.src: - C) Detention charges
segments.tr: - C) Biaya detensi

segments.src: - D) Minimum charge floor
segments.tr: - D) Batas minimum biaya

segments.src: **2.** True or False: Because truckload (TL) service uses a dedicated trailer and skips terminal hubs, it is always the cheaper choice compared to LTL.
segments.tr: **2.** Benar atau Salah: Karena layanan truckload (TL) menggunakan trailer khusus dan melewati hub terminal, layanan ini selalu lebih murah dibandingkan LTL.

segments.src: **3.** A carrier's truck delivers a full load from Atlanta to Nashville, then drives back to Atlanta empty.
segments.tr: **3.** Truk perusahaan angkutan mengirim muatan penuh dari Atlanta ke Nashville, lalu kembali ke Atlanta dalam keadaan kosong.

segments.src: What is that return leg called, and what's the standard fix?
segments.tr: Apa nama perjalanan pulang itu, dan apa solusi standarnya?

segments.src: - A) Detention — reduce dock wait time
segments.tr: - A) Detensi: kurangi waktu tunggu dok

segments.src: - B) Accessorial — renegotiate the fee schedule
segments.tr: - B) Aksesori: negosiasikan ulang jadwal biaya

segments.src: - C) Deadhead — find a backhaul
segments.tr: - C) Deadhead: temukan backhaul

segments.src: - D) Intermodal drayage — switch to rail
segments.tr: - D) Drayase intermodal: beralih ke kereta api

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Linehaul** — The base charge for moving freight between two points, before fuel and add-on fees.
segments.tr: - **Linehaul**: Biaya dasar untuk memindahkan barang antara dua titik, sebelum biaya bahan bakar dan biaya tambahan.

segments.src: - **Accessorial** — Any charge beyond linehaul for extra service: liftgate, residential delivery, detention, redelivery.
segments.tr: - **Aksesori**: Biaya apa pun di luar linehaul untuk layanan tambahan: liftgate, pengiriman ke rumah tinggal, detensi, pengiriman ulang.

segments.src: - **Dimensional (DIM) weight** — Billable weight calculated from a shipment's volume, used when freight is bulky but light.
segments.tr: - **Berat dimensi (DIM)**: Berat yang dapat ditagih, dihitung dari volume pengiriman, digunakan ketika barang besar tetapi ringan.

segments.src: - **Freight class** — The NMFC 50–500 scale that rates LTL freight by density, stowability, handling, and liability.
segments.tr: - **Kelas angkutan**: Skala NMFC 50–500 yang menentukan tarif LTL berdasarkan kepadatan, kemudahan penyusunan, penanganan, dan tanggung jawab.

segments.src: - **Deadhead** — Miles driven with an empty trailer; full cost, zero revenue.
segments.tr: - **Deadhead**: Mil yang ditempuh dengan trailer kosong; biaya penuh, tanpa pendapatan.

segments.src: - **Intermodal** — Moving one container across two or more modes (typically rail for the long haul, truck for the ends) without unpacking it.
segments.tr: - **Intermodal**: Memindahkan satu kontainer melalui dua moda atau lebih (biasanya kereta untuk jarak jauh, truk untuk ujungnya) tanpa membongkarnya.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** Packing peanuts are extremely low-density, so carriers bill on the space consumed rather than the scale weight (dim weight in parcel, high freight class in LTL).
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **1 — B.** Isian busa sangat berkepadatan rendah, jadi perusahaan angkutan menagih berdasarkan ruang yang digunakan, bukan berat timbangan (berat dimensi di parsel, kelas angkutan tinggi di LTL).

segments.src: **2 — False.** TL only wins once your shipment is large enough to justify buying the whole trailer; below the breakeven (commonly ~8–14 pallets), you'd be paying to haul empty space, and LTL's shared-trailer model is cheaper.
segments.tr: **2 — Salah.** TL hanya menang ketika pengiriman Anda cukup besar untuk membenarkan pembelian seluruh trailer. Di bawah titik impas (umumnya ~8–14 palet), Anda membayar untuk mengangkut ruang kosong, dan model trailer bersama LTL lebih murah.

segments.src: **3 — C.** Empty return miles are deadhead, and the standard remedy is securing a backhaul — paying freight for the return leg — which is often a larger saving than negotiating the outbound rate down.*
segments.tr: **3 — C.** Mil pulang yang kosong disebut deadhead, dan solusi standarnya adalah mengamankan backhaul (membayar angkutan untuk perjalanan pulang), yang sering kali menghemat lebih besar daripada menegosiasikan tarif perjalanan berangkat agar turun.*

ja.title: [Logistics 101 #8] 一番安いトラックは、空車で戻らせないトラック

segments.src: > Transportation management is three decisions stacked on top of each other: how you move it (mode), what you pay for it (rate structure), and the order you touch the stops (routing) — and the third one is usually where the money hides.
segments.tr: > 輸送管理は、三つの意思決定が積み重なったものです。どの手段で運ぶか（モード）、いくら払うか（運賃体系）、そして停留地をどの順番で回るか（ルーティング）。三つ目こそ、たいていお金が隠れている場所です。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: Transportation is the single biggest line item in most supply chains.
segments.tr: 輸送は、ほとんどのサプライチェーンで単一で最大のコスト項目です。

segments.src: In the U.S., freight transportation runs well over a trillion dollars a year, and for a typical consumer-goods company, moving product costs more than warehousing it.

segments.src: So "transportation management" isn't a back-office chore.
segments.tr: ですから「輸送管理」は、事務的な雑務ではありません。

segments.src: It's a series of trade-offs a manager makes on purpose.
segments.tr: マネージャーが意図的に下す、一連のトレードオフなのです。

segments.src: **Decision 1: The mode.** Modes line up in a predictable order on cost per ton-mile — pipeline and barge cheapest, then rail, then truck, then air.
segments.tr: **意思決定1：手段（モード）。** 各手段は、トンマイルあたりのコストで予測可能な順に並びます。パイプラインと艀（バージ）が最も安く、次いで鉄道、トラック、航空の順です。

segments.src: Speed lines up in exactly the reverse order.

segments.src: That inversion is the whole game.
segments.tr: この逆転こそが、このゲームの核心です。

segments.src: Air freight can cost 5–10x truck per pound but delivers in a day; ocean can cost a fraction of air but takes weeks.
segments.tr: 航空輸送は、重量あたりでトラックの5～10倍のコストがかかることもありますが、1日で届けてくれます。海上輸送は航空の何分の一かのコストで済みますが、数週間かかります。

segments.src: You aren't picking the "best" mode, you're picking where on that curve your product belongs.
segments.tr: 「最良」の手段を選ぶのではなく、そのカーブ上で製品がどこに位置すべきかを選んでいるのです。

segments.src: Fresh strawberries and replacement heart valves ride at the fast end.
segments.tr: 生いちごや人工心臓弁は、速い側に乗ります。

segments.src: Gravel and canned beans ride at the cheap end.
segments.tr: 砂利や缶詰の豆は、安い側に乗ります。

segments.src: Within trucking there's a second fork most people never see:
segments.tr: トラック輸送の中にも、ほとんどの人が気づかない二つ目の分岐があります：

segments.src: - **Parcel** — anything roughly under 150 lbs, one box at a time (UPS, FedEx, USPS).
segments.tr: - **小口（パーセル）** — おおむね150ポンド以下のもので、一度に一箱ずつ扱います（UPS、FedEx、USPS など）。

segments.src: - **LTL (less-than-truckload)** — a few pallets sharing a trailer with other shippers' freight, moving through terminal hubs.
segments.tr: - **LTL（ロードの一部）** — 他の荷主の貨物と同じトレーラーを分け合う数パレット分の荷物で、ターミナルのハブを経由して運ばれます。

segments.src: - **TL / FTL (truckload)** — you buy the whole trailer, and it drives point to point.
segments.tr: - **TL / FTL（トラック一台分）** — トレーラー一台分をまるごと購入し、出発地から目的地まで直行します。

segments.src: - **Intermodal** — the container rides a train for the long middle, and a truck for the first and last 100 miles.
segments.tr: - **複合輸送（インターモーダル）** — コンテナは長距離の中間区間を鉄道で、最初と最後の100マイルをトラックで運ばれます。

segments.src: **Decision 2: The rate structure.** A freight invoice is almost never one number.
segments.tr: **意思決定2：運賃体系。** 貨物の請求書は、ほとんどの場合一つの数字ではありません。

segments.src: It's a stack:
segments.tr: それは積み重ねです：

segments.src: total = linehaul + fuel surcharge + accessorials + minimum charge floor
segments.tr: total = linehaul + fuel surcharge + accessorials + minimum charge floor

segments.src: *Linehaul* is the base move (distance × weight × lane).
segments.tr: *幹線運賃（リニホール）* は基本の輸送料金です（距離×重量×ルート）。

segments.src: *Fuel surcharge* floats with a published diesel index — the DOE/EIA weekly average — so carriers don't have to re-quote every time fuel moves.
segments.tr: *燃料サーチャージ* は公表されたディーゼル指数（DOE/EIA の週間平均）に連動して変動するため、運送会社は燃料が動くたびに見積もりをやり直す必要がありません。

segments.src: *Accessorials* are the add-ons: liftgate, residential delivery, inside delivery, detention when your dock makes the driver wait, redelivery when nobody's there.
segments.tr: *付帯料金（アクセサリアル）* は追加料金です：テールゲート（リフトゲート）、住宅への配送、屋内への搬入、ドックでドライバーが待たされた場合の待機料（デテンション）、誰も受け取りに来なかった場合の再配達など。

segments.src: Accessorials are where budgets quietly bleed, because nobody quotes them and everybody pays them.
segments.tr: 付帯料金は、予算がひそかに流出する場所です。誰も見積もりに含めず、誰もが支払うからです。

segments.src: Two pricing quirks worth knowing.
segments.tr: 知っておく価値のある運賃の癖が二つあります。

segments.src: First, **dimensional weight**: carriers bill on whichever is greater, actual weight or volume converted to weight.
segments.tr: 一つ目は**容積重量（ディメンショナル・ウェイト）**です：運送会社は、実重量と容積を重量換算した値のうち大きい方で請求します。

segments.src: A big box of pillows takes up trailer space the carrier can't resell, so they charge for the space.
segments.tr: 大きな枕の箱は、運送会社が転売できないトレーラーのスペースを占有するため、そのスペースに対して料金を取るのです。

segments.src: dim weight (lbs) = (L x W x H in inches) / divisor     # 139 is common for U.S. parcel
segments.tr: dim weight (lbs) = (L x W x H in inches) / divisor     # 139 is common for U.S. parcel

segments.src: Second, **freight class**: LTL freight is classified 50 through 500 based on density, stowability, handling, and liability.
segments.tr: 二つ目は**貨物クラス（フレイトクラス）**です：LTL 貨物は、密度、積み付けやすさ、取扱い、責任の度合いに基づいて、50から500までのクラスに分類されます。

segments.src: Class 50 (dense, sturdy, boring — think bricks) is cheap.
segments.tr: クラス50（密度が高く、頑丈で、地味なもの ― レンガのようなもの）は安価です。

segments.src: Class 500 (light, bulky, fragile — think ping-pong balls) is expensive.
segments.tr: クラス500（軽く、かさばり、壊れやすいもの ― ピンポン球のようなもの）は高価です。

segments.src: Same trailer, same 500 miles, wildly different bill.
segments.tr: 同じトレーラー、同じ500マイルでも、請求額はまったく違います。

segments.src: **Decision 3: The route.** This is the hardest one and the most under-managed.
segments.tr: **意思決定3：ルート。** これは最も難しく、最も管理が行き届いていない判断です。

segments.src: Deciding what order to hit 10 stops in isn't a small problem — with a fixed starting depot, there are 10!
segments.tr: 10か所の停留地をどの順番で回るかを決めるのは、小さな問題ではありません。出発の倉庫を固定しても、10!

segments.src: ÷ 2 ≈ **1.8 million** possible route orders.
segments.tr: ÷ 2 ≈ **180万通り**のルート順序があります。

segments.src: Add 20 stops and the count exceeds the number of atoms you'd care to count.
segments.tr: 停留地が20になると、その数は、数えようと思う原子の数を超えます。

segments.src: Computer scientists call this family of problems the Traveling Salesman Problem and its bigger sibling the Vehicle Routing Problem, and both are NP-hard: nobody checks every option, so real software uses heuristics that find a very good route fast rather than the perfect one slowly.
segments.tr: コンピュータ科学者はこの種の問題群を巡回セールスマン問題と呼び、その大型版を配送経路問題（VRP）と呼びます。どちらもNP困難です。すべての選択肢を調べる者はいないので、実際のソフトウェアは、完璧な答えをゆっくり求めるのではなく、非常に良いルートを素早く見つけるヒューリスティクスを使います。

segments.src: Routing also means killing empty miles.
segments.tr: ルーティングは、空車の走行距離を減らすことも意味します。

segments.src: A truck driving back to base with nothing in it is **deadhead** — full cost, zero revenue.
segments.tr: 中身を積まずに拠点へ戻るトラックは**デッドヘッド**です ― 全コストがかかるのに、収益はゼロです。

segments.src: Roughly a sixth of U.S.
segments.tr: 米国のトラック走行距離の

segments.src: truck miles run empty.
segments.tr: おおよそ6分の1は空車で走っています。

segments.src: Finding a **backhaul** (paying freight for the return leg) is often a bigger win than shaving a nickel off the outbound rate.
segments.tr: **バックホール**（帰りの区間にも貨物料金を払って積むこと）を見つけることは、出荷の運賃を数セント削るよりも、しばしば大きな効果があります。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活での例

segments.src: Say you run a small cold-brew coffee company in Portland, Oregon, and you just landed a Chicago account.
segments.tr: オレゴン州ポートランドで、小さなコールドブリューのコーヒー会社を経営していて、シカゴの取引先を新たに獲得したとしましょう。

segments.src: Six pallets, 3,600 lbs total, and it needs to be there in a week.
segments.tr: パレット6枚、合計3,600ポンドで、1週間以内に届ける必要があります。

segments.src: Your options, roughly (illustrative numbers, not quotes):
segments.tr: 選択肢は大まかに以下のとおりです（概算の数字で、見積もりではありません）：

segments.src: - **Parcel**: ship it as ~300 individual cases. Fast, trackable, and you'd pay something like $3,000+ once dim weight kicks in. Parcel punishes you for volume.
segments.tr: - **小口（パーセル）**：約300個の個別のケースとして出荷します。速く、追跡可能ですが、容積重量が適用されると3,000ドル以上かかることもあります。小口輸送は、かさばるほど罰せられます。

segments.src: - **LTL**: six pallets on a shared trailer, ~5–7 days through terminal hubs. Maybe $1,400. But your customer's Lincoln Park storefront has no dock, so add a liftgate fee (~$100) and a limited-access delivery fee (~$90). Your $1,400 quote is a $1,600 invoice.
segments.tr: - **LTL**：6パレットを共有トレーラーで、ターミナルのハブを経由して約5～7日。おそらく1,400ドルです。しかし、取引先のリンカーン・パークの店舗にはドックがないため、テールゲート料金（約100ドル）と、制限区域への配送料金（約90ドル）が加算されます。1,400ドルの見積もりは、1,600ドルの請求書になります。

segments.src: - **Truckload**: you'd buy 2,100 miles of trailer for maybe $4,000. Insane for six pallets — you'd be paying for 20 pallets of empty air.
segments.tr: - **トラック一台分（TL）**：2,100マイル分のトレーラーを、おそらく4,000ドルで購入することになります。6パレットには無謀な選択です。空っぽの空間20パレット分にお金を払うことになります。

segments.src: - **Intermodal**: cheapest per mile, but the container-load economics don't work at six pallets, and the extra transit days eat your buffer.
segments.tr: - **複合輸送（インターモーダル）**：マイルあたりは最も安いですが、6パレットではコンテナ一本分の経済性が成り立たず、余分な輸送日数で余裕が食いつぶされます。

segments.src: LTL wins.
segments.tr: LTLが勝ちます。

segments.src: But notice *why* it wins: not because it's fast or cheap in the abstract, but because your shipment size fell in its sweet spot.
segments.tr: しかし、*なぜ*勝つのかに注目してください：抽象的に速いからでも安いからでもなく、出荷量がLTLのちょうど良い範囲に収まっているからです。

segments.src: Double the order to 14 pallets and truckload suddenly beats it on cost per pallet — that's the classic **LTL/TL breakeven**, usually somewhere around 8–14 pallets depending on the lane.
segments.tr: 注文を14パレットに倍増させると、トラック一台分の方がパレットあたりのコストでLTLを上回ります ― これが典型的な**LTL/TLの損益分岐点**で、ルートによって異なりますが、おおよそ8～14パレットの間にあります。

segments.src: Now the routing half.
segments.tr: 次はルーティングの話です。

segments.src: Once you're delivering to 40 Chicago-area accounts yourself, the question stops being "what's my rate?"
segments.tr: シカゴ近郊の40の取引先に自分で配送するようになると、問いは「料金はいくらか？」ではなくなり、

segments.src: and becomes "what order do I drive?"
segments.tr: 「どの順番で運転すればいいか？」になります。

segments.src: UPS's ORION routing system is the famous version of this: by optimizing driver routes — including the well-known habit of minimizing left turns, which waste time idling in traffic and raise collision risk — UPS has said it saves on the order of 100 million miles a year.
segments.tr: UPSのORIONルーティングシステムは、これの有名な例です。ドライバーのルートを最適化することで ― 交通渋滞でのアイドリングによる時間の浪費や衝突リスクを高める、左折を減らすという有名な傾向も含めて ― UPSは年間およそ1億マイルを節約していると述べています。

segments.src: Nobody negotiated a better fuel price.
segments.tr: 燃料価格を交渉してより良くしたわけではありません。

segments.src: They just drove better sequences.
segments.tr: ただ、より良い順番で走っただけです。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三行まとめ

segments.src: 1. Mode choice is a speed-versus-cost trade: pipeline → rail → truck → air gets faster and more expensive at every step, so match the mode to what the product's time is actually worth.
segments.tr: 1. 手段の選択は、速度とコストのトレードオフです。パイプライン → 鉄道 → トラック → 航空の順に、一段ごとに速くなり、高くなります。ですから、製品の時間が実際にどれだけの価値があるかに手段を合わせましょう。

segments.src: 2. Freight rates are a stack — linehaul, fuel surcharge, accessorials, minimums — and volume-based pricing (dim weight, freight class) means bulky-but-light freight pays like heavy freight.
segments.tr: 2. 運賃は積み重ねです ― 幹線運賃、燃料サーチャージ、付帯料金、最低料金など。そして、容積ベースの料金（容積重量、貨物クラス）は、かさばるが軽い貨物が重い貨物と同じ料金になることを意味します。

segments.src: 3. Routing is a combinatorial problem solved by heuristics, and the biggest lever is usually eliminating empty miles, not shaving the base rate.
segments.tr: 3. ルーティングは、ヒューリスティクスで解かれる組合せ問題です。そして最大のレバーは、通常、基本運賃を数セント削ることではなく、空車の走行距離を減らすことです。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自己確認クイズ

segments.src: **1.** You're shipping 800 lbs of foam packing peanuts across the country.
segments.tr: **1.** あなたは800ポンドの発泡スチロールの梱包材（ピーナッツ）を、国中に出荷しようとしています。

segments.src: Which pricing mechanism will most likely drive your cost above what the scale weight suggests?
segments.tr: 秤の重量が示すよりも、どの料金の仕組みがコストを押し上げる可能性が最も高いでしょうか？

segments.src: - A) Fuel surcharge
segments.tr: - A) 燃料サーチャージ

segments.src: - B) Dimensional weight / high freight class
segments.tr: - B) 容積重量 / 高い貨物クラス

segments.src: - C) Detention charges
segments.tr: - C) 待機料（デテンション）

segments.src: - D) Minimum charge floor
segments.tr: - D) 最低料金の下限

segments.src: **2.** True or False: Because truckload (TL) service uses a dedicated trailer and skips terminal hubs, it is always the cheaper choice compared to LTL.
segments.tr: **2.** 正誤を答えてください：トラック一台分（TL）のサービスは専用のトレーラーを使い、ターミナルのハブを経由しないため、LTLと比べて常に安い選択肢である。

segments.src: **3.** A carrier's truck delivers a full load from Atlanta to Nashville, then drives back to Atlanta empty.
segments.tr: **3.** 運送会社のトラックが、アトランタからナッシュビルまで満載の貨物を届けた後、空車でアトランタに戻ります。

segments.src: What is that return leg called, and what's the standard fix?
segments.tr: その帰りの区間は何と呼ばれ、標準的な解決策は何でしょうか？

segments.src: - A) Detention — reduce dock wait time
segments.tr: - A) 待機料（デテンション）― ドックでの待ち時間を減らす

segments.src: - B) Accessorial — renegotiate the fee schedule
segments.tr: - B) 付帯料金（アクセサリアル）― 料金表を再交渉する

segments.src: - C) Deadhead — find a backhaul
segments.tr: - C) デッドヘッド ― バックホールを見つける

segments.src: - D) Intermodal drayage — switch to rail
segments.tr: - D) インターモーダルのドレージ ― 鉄道に切り替える

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日の用語

segments.src: - **Linehaul** — The base charge for moving freight between two points, before fuel and add-on fees.
segments.tr: - **幹線運賃（リニホール）** — 燃料費や付帯料金を含める前の、二地点間で貨物を運ぶための基本料金。

segments.src: - **Accessorial** — Any charge beyond linehaul for extra service: liftgate, residential delivery, detention, redelivery.
segments.tr: - **付帯料金（アクセサリアル）** — 幹線運賃を超える追加サービスに対する料金：テールゲート、住宅配送、待機料、再配達など。

segments.src: - **Dimensional (DIM) weight** — Billable weight calculated from a shipment's volume, used when freight is bulky but light.
segments.tr: - **容積重量（DIM重量）** — 貨物の容積から算出される請求重量。かさばるが軽い貨物に使われます。

segments.src: - **Freight class** — The NMFC 50–500 scale that rates LTL freight by density, stowability, handling, and liability.
segments.tr: - **貨物クラス（フレイトクラス）** — 密度、積み付けやすさ、取扱い、責任に基づいてLTL貨物を料金付けする、NMFCの50～500の尺度。

segments.src: - **Deadhead** — Miles driven with an empty trailer; full cost, zero revenue.
segments.tr: - **デッドヘッド** — 空のトレーラーで走行する距離。全コストがかかり、収益はゼロ。

segments.src: - **Intermodal** — Moving one container across two or more modes (typically rail for the long haul, truck for the ends) without unpacking it.
segments.tr: - **複合輸送（インターモーダル）** — コンテナを開けずに、二つ以上の手段（通常は長距離は鉄道、両端はトラック）で一つのコンテナを運ぶこと。

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** Packing peanuts are extremely low-density, so carriers bill on the space consumed rather than the scale weight (dim weight in parcel, high freight class in LTL).
segments.tr: *解答：**1 — B。** 梱包用ピーナッツは非常に密度が低いため、運送会社は秤の重量ではなく、占有したスペースに対して請求します（小口では容積重量、LTLでは高い貨物クラス）。

segments.src: **2 — False.** TL only wins once your shipment is large enough to justify buying the whole trailer; below the breakeven (commonly ~8–14 pallets), you'd be paying to haul empty space, and LTL's shared-trailer model is cheaper.
segments.tr: **2 — 誤り。** TLが勝つのは、出荷量がトレーラー一台分を購入するのに十分な大きさになってからです。損益分岐点（一般的に約8～14パレット）未満では、空いた空間を運ぶために料金を払うことになり、LTLの共有トレーラーのモデルの方が安くなります。

segments.src: **3 — C.** Empty return miles are deadhead, and the standard remedy is securing a backhaul — paying freight for the return leg — which is often a larger saving than negotiating the outbound rate down.*
segments.tr: **3 — C。** 空車の帰り道はデッドヘッドで、標準的な対策はバックホールを確保すること ― 帰りの区間にも貨物料金を払うこと ― で、出荷の運賃を値切るよりも大きな節約になることがよくあります。*

de.title: [Logistik 101 #8] Der günstigste Lkw ist der, den du nicht leer zurückschickst

segments.src: > Transportation management is three decisions stacked on top of each other: how you move it (mode), what you pay for it (rate structure), and the order you touch the stops (routing) — and the third one is usually where the money hides.
segments.tr: > Transportmanagement besteht aus drei übereinanderliegenden Entscheidungen: wie du es bewegst (Verkehrsträger), was du dafür bezahlst (Tarifstruktur) und in welcher Reihenfolge du die Stopps anfährst (Routing). Die dritte ist meist der Ort, an dem das Geld versteckt ist.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Heutiges Konzept

segments.src: Transportation is the single biggest line item in most supply chains.
segments.tr: Transport ist in den meisten Lieferketten der einzelne größte Kostenposten.

segments.src: In the U.S., freight transportation runs well over a trillion dollars a year, and for a typical consumer-goods company, moving product costs more than warehousing it.
segments.tr: In den USA macht der Güterverkehr jährlich weit über eine Billion Dollar aus, und für ein typisches Konsumgüterunternehmen kostet der Transport der Ware mehr als deren Lagerung.

segments.src: So "transportation management" isn't a back-office chore.
segments.tr: Transportmanagement ist also keine Routineaufgabe im Backoffice.

segments.src: It's a series of trade-offs a manager makes on purpose.
segments.tr: Es ist eine Reihe von Abwägungen, die eine Führungskraft bewusst trifft.

segments.src: **Decision 1: The mode.** Modes line up in a predictable order on cost per ton-mile — pipeline and barge cheapest, then rail, then truck, then air.
segments.tr: **Entscheidung 1: der Verkehrsträger.** Die Verkehrsträger ordnen sich bei den Kosten pro Tonnenmeile in einer vorhersehbaren Reihenfolge an: Pipeline und Binnenschiff am günstigsten, dann Bahn, dann Lkw, dann Flugzeug.

segments.src: Speed lines up in exactly the reverse order.
segments.tr: Bei der Geschwindigkeit verhält es sich genau umgekehrt.

segments.src: That inversion is the whole game.
segments.tr: Diese Umkehrung ist das ganze Spiel.

segments.src: Air freight can cost 5–10x truck per pound but delivers in a day; ocean can cost a fraction of air but takes weeks.
segments.tr: Luftfracht kann pro Pfund das Fünf- bis Zehnfache eines Lkw kosten, liefert aber in einem Tag; Seefracht kostet einen Bruchteil der Luftfracht, braucht dafür aber Wochen.

segments.src: You aren't picking the "best" mode, you're picking where on that curve your product belongs.
segments.tr: Du wählst nicht den „besten“ Verkehrsträger, sondern bestimmst, wo auf dieser Kurve dein Produkt hingehört.

segments.src: Fresh strawberries and replacement heart valves ride at the fast end.
segments.tr: Frische Erdbeeren und Ersatz-Herzklappen fahren am schnellen Ende.

segments.src: Gravel and canned beans ride at the cheap end.
segments.tr: Schotter und Dosenbohnen fahren am billigen Ende.

segments.src: Within trucking there's a second fork most people never see:
segments.tr: Innerhalb des Lkw-Verkehrs gibt es eine zweite Weggabelung, die die meisten nie sehen:

segments.src: - **Parcel** — anything roughly under 150 lbs, one box at a time (UPS, FedEx, USPS).
segments.tr: - **Paket**: alles bis etwa 150 lbs, ein Karton nach dem anderen (UPS, FedEx, USPS).

segments.src: - **LTL (less-than-truckload)** — a few pallets sharing a trailer with other shippers' freight, moving through terminal hubs.
segments.tr: - **LTL (Teilladung)**: einige Paletten teilen sich einen Anhänger mit der Fracht anderer Versender und laufen über Terminal-Hubs.

segments.src: - **TL / FTL (truckload)** — you buy the whole trailer, and it drives point to point.
segments.tr: - **TL / FTL (Komplettladung)**: du kaufst den gesamten Anhänger, und er fährt direkt von Punkt zu Punkt.

segments.src: - **Intermodal** — the container rides a train for the long middle, and a truck for the first and last 100 miles.
segments.tr: - **Intermodal**: der Container fährt für den langen Mittelteil per Bahn, für die ersten und letzten 100 Meilen per Lkw.

segments.src: **Decision 2: The rate structure.** A freight invoice is almost never one number.
segments.tr: **Entscheidung 2: die Tarifstruktur.** Eine Frachtrechnung besteht fast nie aus einer einzigen Zahl.

segments.src: It's a stack:
segments.tr: Sie ist ein Stapel:

segments.src: total = linehaul + fuel surcharge + accessorials + minimum charge floor
segments.tr: total = linehaul + fuel surcharge + accessorials + minimum charge floor

segments.src: *Linehaul* is the base move (distance × weight × lane).
segments.tr: *Linehaul* ist die Grundstrecke (Entfernung × Gewicht × Relation).

segments.src: *Fuel surcharge* floats with a published diesel index — the DOE/EIA weekly average — so carriers don't have to re-quote every time fuel moves.
segments.tr: *Treibstoffzuschlag* schwankt mit einem veröffentlichten Dieselindex, dem wöchentlichen Durchschnitt von DOE/EIA, damit Frachtführer nicht bei jeder Treibstoffpreisänderung neu kalkulieren müssen.

segments.src: *Accessorials* are the add-ons: liftgate, residential delivery, inside delivery, detention when your dock makes the driver wait, redelivery when nobody's there.
segments.tr: *Nebenkosten (Accessorials)* sind die Zusatzleistungen: Hebebühne, Zustellung an Privatadressen, Zustellung in die Wohnung, Standzeiten (Detention), wenn deine Rampe den Fahrer warten lässt, erneute Zustellung, wenn niemand angetroffen wird.

segments.src: Accessorials are where budgets quietly bleed, because nobody quotes them and everybody pays them.
segments.tr: Bei den Nebenkosten fließt Budget unbemerkt ab, weil sie niemand einplant und trotzdem alle zahlen.

segments.src: Two pricing quirks worth knowing.
segments.tr: Zwei Preiseigenheiten lohnen sich zu kennen.

segments.src: First, **dimensional weight**: carriers bill on whichever is greater, actual weight or volume converted to weight.
segments.tr: Erstens das **Dimensionsgewicht**: Frachtführer berechnen nach dem jeweils höheren Wert, entweder dem tatsächlichen Gewicht oder dem in Gewicht umgerechneten Volumen.

segments.src: A big box of pillows takes up trailer space the carrier can't resell, so they charge for the space.
segments.tr: Ein großer Karton mit Kissen belegt Anhängerfläche, die der Frachtführer nicht weiterverkaufen kann, also berechnet er den Platz.

segments.src: dim weight (lbs) = (L x W x H in inches) / divisor     # 139 is common for U.S. parcel
segments.tr: dim weight (lbs) = (L x W x H in inches) / divisor     # 139 is common for U.S. parcel

segments.src: Second, **freight class**: LTL freight is classified 50 through 500 based on density, stowability, handling, and liability.
segments.tr: Zweitens die **Frachtklasse**: LTL-Fracht wird von 50 bis 500 klassifiziert, abhängig von Dichte, Stapelbarkeit, Handhabung und Haftung.

segments.src: Class 50 (dense, sturdy, boring — think bricks) is cheap.
segments.tr: Klasse 50 (dicht, robust, unspektakulär, denk an Ziegel) ist günstig.

segments.src: Class 500 (light, bulky, fragile — think ping-pong balls) is expensive.
segments.tr: Klasse 500 (leicht, sperrig, zerbrechlich, denk an Tischtennisbälle) ist teuer.

segments.src: Same trailer, same 500 miles, wildly different bill.
segments.tr: Gleicher Anhänger, gleiche 500 Meilen, völlig unterschiedliche Rechnung.

segments.src: **Decision 3: The route.** This is the hardest one and the most under-managed.
segments.tr: **Entscheidung 3: die Route.** Das ist die schwierigste und am wenigsten gesteuerte Entscheidung.

segments.src: Deciding what order to hit 10 stops in isn't a small problem — with a fixed starting depot, there are 10!
segments.tr: Die Reihenfolge, in der du 10 Stopps anfährst, ist kein kleines Problem. Bei einem festen Startdepot gibt es 10!

segments.src: ÷ 2 ≈ **1.8 million** possible route orders.
segments.tr: ÷ 2 ≈ **1,8 Millionen** mögliche Routenreihenfolgen.

segments.src: Add 20 stops and the count exceeds the number of atoms you'd care to count.
segments.tr: Bei 20 Stopps übersteigt die Anzahl die Zahl der Atome, die man sinnvoll zählen möchte.

segments.src: Computer scientists call this family of problems the Traveling Salesman Problem and its bigger sibling the Vehicle Routing Problem, and both are NP-hard: nobody checks every option, so real software uses heuristics that find a very good route fast rather than the perfect one slowly.
segments.tr: Informatiker nennen diese Problemfamilie das Problem des Handlungsreisenden (Traveling Salesman Problem) und seinen größeren Verwandten das Fahrzeugroutenproblem (Vehicle Routing Problem). Beide sind NP-schwer: Niemand prüft jede Option, daher verwendet echte Software Heuristiken, die schnell eine sehr gute Route finden, statt langsam die perfekte.

segments.src: Routing also means killing empty miles.
segments.tr: Routing bedeutet auch, Leerkilometer zu vermeiden.

segments.src: A truck driving back to base with nothing in it is **deadhead** — full cost, zero revenue.
segments.tr: Ein Lkw, der leer zur Basis zurückfährt, ist **Leerfahrt (Deadhead)**: volle Kosten, null Erlös.

segments.src: Roughly a sixth of U.S.
segments.tr: Etwa ein Sechstel der Lkw-Kilometer in den USA

segments.src: truck miles run empty.
segments.tr: fährt leer.

segments.src: Finding a **backhaul** (paying freight for the return leg) is often a bigger win than shaving a nickel off the outbound rate.
segments.tr: Eine **Rückladung (Backhaul)** zu finden, also Fracht für die Rückstrecke zu bezahlen, ist oft ein größerer Gewinn, als fünf Cent vom Hinfahrtpreis abzuziehen.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Say you run a small cold-brew coffee company in Portland, Oregon, and you just landed a Chicago account.
segments.tr: Angenommen, du betreibst eine kleine Cold-Brew-Kaffeerösterei in Portland, Oregon, und hast gerade einen Kunden in Chicago gewonnen.

segments.src: Six pallets, 3,600 lbs total, and it needs to be there in a week.
segments.tr: Sechs Paletten, insgesamt 3.600 lbs, und sie müssen innerhalb einer Woche ankommen.

segments.src: Your options, roughly (illustrative numbers, not quotes):
segments.tr: Deine Optionen, grob (veranschaulichende Zahlen, keine Angebote):

segments.src: - **Parcel**: ship it as ~300 individual cases. Fast, trackable, and you'd pay something like $3,000+ once dim weight kicks in. Parcel punishes you for volume.
segments.tr: - **Paket**: Versand als etwa 300 einzelne Kartons. Schnell, nachverfolgbar, und du zahlst etwa 3.000 $+, sobald das Dimensionsgewicht greift. Paket bestraft dich für Volumen.

segments.src: - **LTL**: six pallets on a shared trailer, ~5–7 days through terminal hubs. Maybe $1,400. But your customer's Lincoln Park storefront has no dock, so add a liftgate fee (~$100) and a limited-access delivery fee (~$90). Your $1,400 quote is a $1,600 invoice.
segments.tr: - **LTL**: sechs Paletten auf einem geteilten Anhänger, etwa 5–7 Tage über Terminal-Hubs. Vielleicht 1.400 $. Doch der Laden deines Kunden in Lincoln Park hat keine Rampe, also kommt eine Hebebühnengebühr (~100 $) und eine Gebühr für eingeschränkt zugängliche Zustellung (~90 $) hinzu. Dein Angebot über 1.400 $ wird zu einer Rechnung über 1.600 $.

segments.src: - **Truckload**: you'd buy 2,100 miles of trailer for maybe $4,000. Insane for six pallets — you'd be paying for 20 pallets of empty air.
segments.tr: - **Komplettladung**: du würdest 2.100 Meilen Anhängerfläche für vielleicht 4.000 $ kaufen. Absurd für sechs Paletten, denn du würdest für 20 Paletten leere Luft bezahlen.

segments.src: - **Intermodal**: cheapest per mile, but the container-load economics don't work at six pallets, and the extra transit days eat your buffer.
segments.tr: - **Intermodal**: am günstigsten pro Meile, aber die Containerladungs-Wirtschaftlichkeit geht bei sechs Paletten nicht auf, und die zusätzlichen Transittage fressen deinen Puffer auf.

segments.src: LTL wins.
segments.tr: LTL gewinnt.

segments.src: But notice *why* it wins: not because it's fast or cheap in the abstract, but because your shipment size fell in its sweet spot.
segments.tr: Aber beachte, *warum* es gewinnt: nicht weil es abstrakt schnell oder günstig ist, sondern weil deine Sendungsgröße in seinen Sweet Spot fällt.

segments.src: Double the order to 14 pallets and truckload suddenly beats it on cost per pallet — that's the classic **LTL/TL breakeven**, usually somewhere around 8–14 pallets depending on the lane.
segments.tr: Verdopple die Bestellung auf 14 Paletten, und die Komplettladung schlägt es plötzlich bei den Kosten pro Palette. Das ist der klassische **LTL/TL-Break-even**, meist irgendwo bei 8–14 Paletten, je nach Relation.

segments.src: Now the routing half.
segments.tr: Nun zur Routing-Hälfte.

segments.src: Once you're delivering to 40 Chicago-area accounts yourself, the question stops being "what's my rate?"
segments.tr: Sobald du selbst 40 Kunden im Großraum Chicago beliefert, lautet die Frage nicht mehr "Was ist mein Tarif?"

segments.src: and becomes "what order do I drive?"
segments.tr: sondern "In welcher Reihenfolge fahre ich?"

segments.src: UPS's ORION routing system is the famous version of this: by optimizing driver routes — including the well-known habit of minimizing left turns, which waste time idling in traffic and raise collision risk — UPS has said it saves on the order of 100 million miles a year.
segments.tr: Das UPS-Routingsystem ORION ist die bekannteste Version davon: Durch die Optimierung der Fahrerrouten, einschließlich der bekannten Gewohnheit, Linksabbiegen zu minimieren, weil dabei Zeit im Stau verschwendet wird und das Unfallrisiko steigt, hat UPS nach eigenen Angaben jährlich etwa 100 Millionen Meilen eingespart.

segments.src: Nobody negotiated a better fuel price.
segments.tr: Niemand hat einen besseren Treibstoffpreis ausgehandelt.

segments.src: They just drove better sequences.
segments.tr: Sie sind einfach bessere Abfolgen gefahren.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in drei Zeilen

segments.src: 1. Mode choice is a speed-versus-cost trade: pipeline → rail → truck → air gets faster and more expensive at every step, so match the mode to what the product's time is actually worth.
segments.tr: 1. Die Wahl des Verkehrsträgers ist ein Abwägen zwischen Geschwindigkeit und Kosten: Pipeline → Bahn → Lkw → Flugzeug wird mit jedem Schritt schneller und teurer, also den Verkehrsträger an den tatsächlichen Wert der Zeit für das Produkt anpassen.

segments.src: 2. Freight rates are a stack — linehaul, fuel surcharge, accessorials, minimums — and volume-based pricing (dim weight, freight class) means bulky-but-light freight pays like heavy freight.
segments.tr: 2. Frachttarife sind ein Stapel aus Linehaul, Treibstoffzuschlag, Nebenkosten und Mindestbeträgen. Volumenbasierte Preise (Dimensionsgewicht, Frachtklasse) bedeuten, dass sperrige, aber leichte Fracht wie schwere Fracht bezahlt wird.

segments.src: 3. Routing is a combinatorial problem solved by heuristics, and the biggest lever is usually eliminating empty miles, not shaving the base rate.
segments.tr: 3. Routing ist ein kombinatorisches Problem, das durch Heuristiken gelöst wird, und der größte Hebel ist meist das Vermeiden von Leerkilometern, nicht das Drücken des Grundtarifs.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Selbsttest

segments.src: **1.** You're shipping 800 lbs of foam packing peanuts across the country.
segments.tr: **1.** Du versendest 800 lbs Schaumstoff-Füllchips quer durchs Land.

segments.src: Which pricing mechanism will most likely drive your cost above what the scale weight suggests?
segments.tr: Welcher Preismechanismus lässt deine Kosten wahrscheinlich über das Gewicht laut Waage steigen?

segments.src: - A) Fuel surcharge
segments.tr: - A) Treibstoffzuschlag

segments.src: - B) Dimensional weight / high freight class
segments.tr: - B) Dimensionsgewicht / hohe Frachtklasse

segments.src: - C) Detention charges
segments.tr: - C) Standzeitgebühren

segments.src: - D) Minimum charge floor
segments.tr: - D) Mindestbetrag

segments.src: **2.** True or False: Because truckload (TL) service uses a dedicated trailer and skips terminal hubs, it is always the cheaper choice compared to LTL.
segments.tr: **2.** Wahr oder falsch: Da der Komplettladungsservice (TL) einen eigenen Anhänger nutzt und Terminal-Hubs auslässt, ist er im Vergleich zu LTL immer die günstigere Wahl.

segments.src: **3.** A carrier's truck delivers a full load from Atlanta to Nashville, then drives back to Atlanta empty.
segments.tr: **3.** Der Lkw eines Frachtführers liefert eine volle Ladung von Atlanta nach Nashville und fährt dann leer nach Atlanta zurück.

segments.src: What is that return leg called, and what's the standard fix?
segments.tr: Wie heißt diese Rückstrecke, und was ist die übliche Lösung?

segments.src: - A) Detention — reduce dock wait time
segments.tr: - A) Standzeit: Wartezeit an der Rampe verkürzen

segments.src: - B) Accessorial — renegotiate the fee schedule
segments.tr: - B) Nebenkosten: Gebührenkatalog neu verhandeln

segments.src: - C) Deadhead — find a backhaul
segments.tr: - C) Leerfahrt (Deadhead): eine Rückladung finden

segments.src: - D) Intermodal drayage — switch to rail
segments.tr: - D) Intermodaler Vorlauf: auf Bahn umsteigen

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Begriffe dieser Lektion

segments.src: - **Linehaul** — The base charge for moving freight between two points, before fuel and add-on fees.
segments.tr: - **Linehaul**: Der Grundtarif für den Transport von Fracht zwischen zwei Punkten, vor Treibstoff und Zusatzgebühren.

segments.src: - **Accessorial** — Any charge beyond linehaul for extra service: liftgate, residential delivery, detention, redelivery.
segments.tr: - **Accessorial (Nebenkosten)**: Jede Gebühr über den Linehaul hinaus für zusätzliche Leistungen: Hebebühne, Zustellung an Privatadressen, Standzeit, erneute Zustellung.

segments.src: - **Dimensional (DIM) weight** — Billable weight calculated from a shipment's volume, used when freight is bulky but light.
segments.tr: - **Dimensionsgewicht (DIM-Gewicht)**: Abrechenbares Gewicht, berechnet aus dem Volumen einer Sendung; wird verwendet, wenn die Fracht sperrig, aber leicht ist.

segments.src: - **Freight class** — The NMFC 50–500 scale that rates LTL freight by density, stowability, handling, and liability.
segments.tr: - **Frachtklasse**: Die NMFC-Skala von 50–500, nach der LTL-Fracht nach Dichte, Stapelbarkeit, Handhabung und Haftung eingestuft wird.

segments.src: - **Deadhead** — Miles driven with an empty trailer; full cost, zero revenue.
segments.tr: - **Leerfahrt (Deadhead)**: Mit leerem Anhänger gefahrene Meilen; volle Kosten, null Erlös.

segments.src: - **Intermodal** — Moving one container across two or more modes (typically rail for the long haul, truck for the ends) without unpacking it.
segments.tr: - **Intermodal**: Transport eines Containers über zwei oder mehr Verkehrsträger (meist Bahn für die Langstrecke, Lkw für die Enden), ohne ihn auszupacken.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** Packing peanuts are extremely low-density, so carriers bill on the space consumed rather than the scale weight (dim weight in parcel, high freight class in LTL).
segments.tr: *Antworten: **1 — B.** Füllchips haben eine extrem geringe Dichte, daher berechnen Frachtführer den belegten Platz statt des Gewichts laut Waage (Dimensionsgewicht bei Paket, hohe Frachtklasse bei LTL).

segments.src: **2 — False.** TL only wins once your shipment is large enough to justify buying the whole trailer; below the breakeven (commonly ~8–14 pallets), you'd be paying to haul empty space, and LTL's shared-trailer model is cheaper.
segments.tr: **2 — Falsch.** TL lohnt sich erst, wenn deine Sendung groß genug ist, um den gesamten Anhänger zu rechtfertigen. Unterhalb des Break-even (meist ~8–14 Paletten) würdest du für leeren Raum bezahlen, und das Modell des geteilten Anhängers bei LTL ist günstiger.

segments.src: **3 — C.** Empty return miles are deadhead, and the standard remedy is securing a backhaul — paying freight for the return leg — which is often a larger saving than negotiating the outbound rate down.*
segments.tr: **3 — C.** Leere Rückfahrt-Kilometer sind Leerfahrt (Deadhead), und die übliche Abhilfe ist die Sicherung einer Rückladung, also Fracht für die Rückstrecke zu bezahlen. Das bringt oft eine größere Ersparnis als das Drücken des Hinfahrtpreises.*

vi.title: [Logistics 101 #8] Chiếc xe tải rẻ nhất là chiếc không bao giờ chạy về rỗng

segments.src: > Transportation management is three decisions stacked on top of each other: how you move it (mode), what you pay for it (rate structure), and the order you touch the stops (routing) — and the third one is usually where the money hides.
segments.tr: > Quản lý vận tải gồm ba quyết định xếp chồng lên nhau: vận chuyển bằng phương thức nào (mode), trả giá theo cấu trúc cước nào (rate structure), và thứ tự ghé các điểm dừng (routing). Quyết định thứ ba thường là nơi tiền bị thất thoát.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: Transportation is the single biggest line item in most supply chains.
segments.tr: Vận tải thường là khoản chi lớn nhất trong hầu hết chuỗi cung ứng.

segments.src: In the U.S., freight transportation runs well over a trillion dollars a year, and for a typical consumer-goods company, moving product costs more than warehousing it.
segments.tr: Tại Hoa Kỳ, chi phí vận tải hàng hóa vượt xa một nghìn tỷ đô la mỗi năm, và với một công ty hàng tiêu dùng điển hình, chi phí vận chuyển sản phẩm còn cao hơn chi phí lưu kho.

segments.src: So "transportation management" isn't a back-office chore.
segments.tr: Vì vậy “quản lý vận tải” không phải là công việc hậu cần vặt vãnh.

segments.src: It's a series of trade-offs a manager makes on purpose.
segments.tr: Đó là chuỗi các sự đánh đổi mà nhà quản lý chủ động đưa ra.

segments.src: **Decision 1: The mode.** Modes line up in a predictable order on cost per ton-mile — pipeline and barge cheapest, then rail, then truck, then air.
segments.tr: **Quyết định 1: Phương thức vận chuyển (mode).** Các phương thức xếp theo thứ tự có thể đoán trước về chi phí trên mỗi tấn-dặm: đường ống và sà lan rẻ nhất, rồi đến đường sắt, đường bộ, và đường hàng không đắt nhất.

segments.src: Speed lines up in exactly the reverse order.
segments.tr: Tốc độ thì xếp theo thứ tự ngược lại.

segments.src: That inversion is the whole game.
segments.tr: Chính sự đảo ngược này là bản chất của cả cuộc chơi.

segments.src: Air freight can cost 5–10x truck per pound but delivers in a day; ocean can cost a fraction of air but takes weeks.
segments.tr: Vận chuyển hàng không có thể đắt gấp 5–10 lần đường bộ tính theo pound nhưng giao trong một ngày; đường biển rẻ hơn hàng không nhiều lần nhưng mất vài tuần.

segments.src: You aren't picking the "best" mode, you're picking where on that curve your product belongs.
segments.tr: Bạn không chọn phương thức “tốt nhất”, mà chọn vị trí của sản phẩm trên đường cong đó.

segments.src: Fresh strawberries and replacement heart valves ride at the fast end.
segments.tr: Dâu tây tươi và van tim thay thế đi ở đầu nhanh.

segments.src: Gravel and canned beans ride at the cheap end.
segments.tr: Sỏi và đậu đóng hộp đi ở đầu rẻ.

segments.src: Within trucking there's a second fork most people never see:
segments.tr: Trong vận tải đường bộ còn có một nhánh thứ hai mà hầu hết mọi người không để ý:

segments.src: - **Parcel** — anything roughly under 150 lbs, one box at a time (UPS, FedEx, USPS).
segments.tr: - **Parcel (kiện nhỏ)**: hàng dưới khoảng 150 lb, từng thùng một (UPS, FedEx, USPS).

segments.src: - **LTL (less-than-truckload)** — a few pallets sharing a trailer with other shippers' freight, moving through terminal hubs.
segments.tr: - **LTL (hàng lẻ, không đủ một xe tải)**: vài pallet ghép chung thùng xe với hàng của các chủ hàng khác, đi qua các trung tâm trung chuyển.

segments.src: - **TL / FTL (truckload)** — you buy the whole trailer, and it drives point to point.
segments.tr: - **TL / FTL (nguyên xe tải)**: bạn thuê cả thùng xe, và xe chạy thẳng từ điểm này đến điểm kia.

segments.src: - **Intermodal** — the container rides a train for the long middle, and a truck for the first and last 100 miles.
segments.tr: - **Intermodal (đa phương thức)**: container đi bằng tàu hỏa cho chặng dài ở giữa, và đi bằng xe tải cho 100 dặm đầu và cuối.

segments.src: **Decision 2: The rate structure.** A freight invoice is almost never one number.
segments.tr: **Quyết định 2: Cấu trúc cước (rate structure).** Hóa đơn vận tải hầu như không bao giờ là một con số duy nhất.

segments.src: It's a stack:
segments.tr: Nó là một chồng các khoản:

segments.tr: total = linehaul + fuel surcharge + accessorials + minimum charge floor

segments.src: *Linehaul* is the base move (distance × weight × lane).
segments.tr: *Linehaul (cước chặng chính)* là chi phí vận chuyển cơ bản (khoảng cách × trọng lượng × tuyến).

segments.src: *Fuel surcharge* floats with a published diesel index — the DOE/EIA weekly average — so carriers don't have to re-quote every time fuel moves.
segments.tr: *Phụ phí nhiên liệu* biến động theo chỉ số dầu diesel được công bố, tức mức trung bình hằng tuần của DOE/EIA, nên các hãng vận tải không phải báo giá lại mỗi khi giá nhiên liệu thay đổi.

segments.src: *Accessorials* are the add-ons: liftgate, residential delivery, inside delivery, detention when your dock makes the driver wait, redelivery when nobody's there.
segments.tr: *Accessorial (phí dịch vụ kèm theo)* là các khoản cộng thêm: thang nâng (liftgate), giao hàng tận nhà dân, giao vào trong nhà, detention (phí chờ khi bến của bạn khiến tài xế phải đợi), và redelivery (giao lại khi không có ai nhận).

segments.src: Accessorials are where budgets quietly bleed, because nobody quotes them and everybody pays them.
segments.tr: Các khoản phí dịch vụ kèm theo chính là nơi ngân sách bị rò rỉ âm thầm, vì không ai báo trước chúng nhưng ai cũng phải trả.

segments.src: Two pricing quirks worth knowing.
segments.tr: Có hai điểm đặc biệt trong định giá đáng biết.

segments.tr: Thứ nhất là **trọng lượng quy đổi theo thể tích (dimensional weight)**: hãng vận tải tính cước theo giá trị lớn hơn giữa trọng lượng thực tế và thể tích quy đổi ra trọng lượng.

segments.src: A big box of pillows takes up trailer space the carrier can't resell, so they charge for the space.
segments.tr: Một thùng lớn đựng gối chiếm chỗ trên xe mà hãng vận tải không thể bán lại, nên họ tính tiền cho khoảng không gian đó.
